title: The Wolf in Sheep's Clothing
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Wolf resolved to disguise himself in order that he might prey upon a flock of sheep without fear of detection. So he clothed himself in a sheepskin, and slipped among the sheep when they were out at pasture. He completely deceived the shepherd, and when the flock was penned for the night he was shut in with the rest. But that very night as it happened, the shepherd, requiring a supply of mutton for the table, laid hands on the Wolf in mistake for a Sheep, and killed him with his knife on the spot.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did the Wolf resolve to disguise himself?
options: So he might prey upon a flock of sheep without fear of detection
So he could escape from a group of hunters
So the shepherd would give him shelter for the winter
So other wolves would not recognize him

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Wolf clothe himself in?
options: A sheepskin
A shepherd's cloak
A bundle of wool
A dog's collar

questions.prompt: According to the passage, when did the Wolf slip among the sheep?
options: When they were out at pasture
While they slept in the fold
As they were being sheared
During a storm at night

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who did the Wolf's disguise completely deceive?
options: The shepherd
The sheep dog
Another wolf
A passing hunter

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the Wolf when the flock was penned for the night?
options: He was shut in with the rest of the sheep
He escaped before the gate closed
He was left outside the pen
He was recognized and driven away

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did the shepherd go into the pen that night?
options: He required a supply of mutton for the table
He wanted to count the sheep before bed
He suspected a wolf had gotten in
He needed to check on a sick lamb

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the shepherd end up killing the Wolf instead of a real sheep?
options: The Wolf's disguise was so complete that the shepherd could not tell him apart from the sheep even up close
The shepherd had discovered the Wolf's true identity beforehand
The Wolf attacked the shepherd first and was killed in self-defense
The shepherd intended to kill the Wolf all along as a trap

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: A disguise meant to deceive others for one's own gain can just as easily bring about one's own ruin
Shepherds are always more clever than wolves
Sheep are safer at pasture than penned for the night
Wolves should never attempt to disguise themselves as sheep

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Wolf plan to prey upon?
options: A flock of sheep
A herd of goats
A pack of hunting dogs
A group of shepherds

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the shepherd do with the Wolf, thinking he was a sheep?
options: Laid hands on him in mistake for a Sheep
Sheared him along with the flock
Marked him with the flock's brand
Led him out to a separate pen

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the shepherd kill the Wolf?
options: With his knife, on the spot
By setting dogs on him
By trapping him in a pit
By calling for other shepherds to help

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what irony lies at the heart of the Wolf's fate?
options: The very disguise the Wolf used to prey on sheep is what led to him being killed as one
The Wolf was killed by another wolf disguised in the same way
The shepherd had planned to kill a wolf all along, not a sheep
The sheep themselves exposed the Wolf's disguise to the shepherd

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "detection" mean in "without fear of detection"?
options: Being discovered or found out
Being punished for a crime
Being followed by hunters
Being rejected by the flock

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Wolf disguises himself as a sheep to prey on the flock, but is mistaken for a sheep himself and killed by the shepherd
A Wolf disguises himself as a shepherd to steal sheep undetected
A shepherd discovers the Wolf's disguise and drives him away before any harm is done
A Wolf befriends the sheep after revealing his true identity to them
